quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can get a ticket.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Drive slower in rain to avoid hydroplaning. If you go too fast, your tires may ride on water and lose grip on the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: How do you safely enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make the other vehicles move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes, check for traffic behind and to the side of your vehicle. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the first car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is dangerous because of high-speed traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the way is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross the centerline to pass. You can pass on the left if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What should you do before you start driving?

options.text: Recline your seat.
Kick the tires.
Adjust your seat and mirrors.

questions.explanation: Before driving, adjust your seat and mirrors so you can see properly. Make sure all passengers wear seat belts. Have your driver license and vehicle registration with you.

questions.question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch far ahead for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles entering at on-ramps and be prepared for sudden changes in traffic flow.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning right?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times. You must let them cross before you turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed. It is a traffic law sign that you must obey.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see if another vehicle is in your blind spot. This helps you avoid hitting a car that is trying to move into the same lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the engine.

questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal or brake to help your vehicle regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to get control of your vehicle back.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear from the truck driver's view or are so close that the driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to drive safely behind the truck.
Are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear from the truck driver's view or are so close that the driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where a car is so close to a truck that it limits the truck driver's ability to stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Children under the age of ____ should not ride in the front seat of a car.
questions.explanation: Children under 13 should sit in the back seat with a seatbelt or child safety seat. The front seat is not safe for them because of the airbag.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming. Check your brakes before going down.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead as you can during the day. Headlights from other cars can also create glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance lane to speed up and match the flow of traffic. Then smoothly merge into the highway. Do not stop or slow down when entering.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and grip the steering wheel firmly. Take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Lightly brake when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until your car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull over and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What lights should you use to see better in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a broken traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
You don't need to stop if the intersection is empty.
Drive fast through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is broken, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Stop completely, look both ways, and let other drivers go first before you enter.

questions.question: When using an exit lane to leave a road, what should you do?

options.text: Don't use your turn signal until you are in the exit lane.
Don't follow the posted speed limits unless the road is wet.
Don't slow down until you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't slow down until you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Start slowing down once you enter the exit lane. Keep your normal speed on the main road so you don't slow down traffic. Then decrease speed gradually on the exit ramp.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads. Cold air flows under bridges, making them icy when surrounding roads are still dry.
